name: Silence Group
keyCapabilities: Exploitation of remote services (SMB, RDP, WMI)
Supply chain compromise via firmware updates
Modification of APT28 exploits for banking targets
Reverse engineering and learning from other threat groups
Targeted attacks on AWS CBR, ATMs, and card processing systems
Deployment of custom backdoor using Russian-language commands
Use of legitimate commercial tools (PowerShell, BITSAdmin, schtasks, ADFind)
Dynamic command & control via domain generation algorithms
recommendedActions: Deploy advanced email filtering and attachment sandboxing to block spear‑phishing attachments.
Enforce least‑privilege access controls and monitor for anomalous use of local accounts.
Permanently patch or harden systems against known CVEs (e.g., Netwrix Auditor, Cisco SD‑WAN/Firepower).
Implement network segmentation and continuous monitoring for suspicious command execution patterns such as Russian-language syntax.
Enable logging and alerting on scheduled task creation, WMI queries, and rundll32 usage.
Regularly scan endpoints for custom downloader binaries (Truebot) and associated persistence mechanisms.
Educate banking staff on recognizing phishing attempts targeting financial operations.
campaignsText: Silence Group operates with a moderate but consistent cadence, typically initiating phishing or vulnerability‑based attacks on financial and governmental targets across Eastern Europe, Central Asia, and North America. Their campaign patterns incorporate learning from more established actors (APT28) and adopting supply‑chain tactics to broaden reach. Recent activity in August 2022 shows a shift toward Truebot delivery systems exploiting high‑profile CVEs. While the group has demonstrated persistence through scheduled tasks and WMI-based persistence, operational tempo remains primarily opportunistic rather than highly orchestrated.
description: Silence Group is a Russian‑state-sponsored threat actor focused on espionage and financial theft against banking and critical infrastructure across Eastern Europe and other regions. Using sophisticated phishing, valid local accounts, remote service exploitation, and custom malware such as Truebot and Grace, the group achieves persistent access and exfiltrates data or funds. Their operations exhibit a blend of supply‑chain attacks, vulnerability exploitation, and targeted payload delivery via downloader tools.
goals: Silence Group primarily seeks espionage and financial gain by infiltrating banking institutions, payment processors, and critical infrastructure. Through sophisticated phishing campaigns and exploitation of remote services or CVEs, they establish footholds and exfiltrate valuable data, including customer information, login credentials, and proprietary technology. The actor also demonstrates an appetite for monetization via ransomware attacks on ATM networks and card‑processing systems, aiming to secure both monetary assets and strategic intelligence.
